学生是高校的中心利益相关者,宁波诺丁汉大学要面向学生、服务学生,保障学生的合法权益,提供良好的学习生活环境,帮助学生全面发展。
教职员工与高校存在雇佣关系,高校要尊重员工、关心员工,为员工提供良好工作环境、合理薪酬和发展空间。
政府对高校施加政策影响,提供资金支持,高校要遵守政策法规,配合政府工作。
行业组织能为高校提供政策信息、行业交流平台,高校应主动参与行业交流。
合作院校是高校开展教学科研合作的对象,要加强沟通交流,实现优势互补。
毕业生对母校形象有重要影响,高校要加强校友联系,提供就业支持。
供货商为高校提供产品和服务,高校应按合同约定提供反馈和评价。
捐赠者和赞助商为高校发展提供资金支持,高校要善用资金,并给予公开表彰。
就业单位是毕业生就业的主要去向,高校要了解需求,改进人才培养。
行业企业提供高校实习实训基地,高校要提供优秀实习生,进行技术转移。
家长关心子女在校学习生活,高校要建立家长沟通机制,接受建议。
地方政府与社区关系到高校融入发展,高校应积极履行社会责任。
学校成立科研管理部门,负责研究生科研管理工作,制定科研项目管理制度,建立科研项目台账。
科研管理部门统筹安排科研经费,负责招标采购办公用房、仪器设备,组织验收科研仪器设备。
学校要建立科研项目过程管理制度,对项目进展进行检查考核。项目结题要提供成果文献、结题报告。
学校要建立科研成果考核评价体系,建立论文质量评价标准,定期开展科研成果评议。
学校要加强对研究生的科研工作指导,组建导师队伍,建立导师考核制度。导师要指导研究生进行文献检索、论文写作。
学校要建立研究生论文管理制度,论文写作应遵循学术规范,杜绝抄袭行为。论文答辩应公开进行,确保质量。
学校要建立知识产权管理制度,鼓励教师申请专利,保护知识产权。
学校要建立科研成果转化机制,选聘科技成果转化专家,促进成果产业化。
学校要建立科研奖励机制,对高水平科研成果给予奖励。组织评选优秀科研成果,进行表彰奖励。问卷采用匿名方式作答，数据仅用于学术研究。问卷设计主要根据Astin的l-E-0模型，分为四个部分的内容。问卷效度方面考虑了内容效度与建构效度。研究对象为宁波诺丁汉大学的大二、大三、大四学生。问卷共发放了269份，回收了253份，有效回收率为87.7%。此外，研究者还进行了访谈，将访谈资料进行整理与分析。
问卷的目的是研究中外合作大学本科生的就读体验。通过收集问卷数据和进行深入交谈，研究人员希望了解学生对学校的看法、学习经历以及与同伴、教师和学校环境的互动等方面的体验。通过分析问卷结果，研究人员将得出对中外合作大学本科生就读体验的结论和结论。
研究表明宁波诺丁汉大学本科生的就读体验整体上处于中等偏上水平。在性别、年级、生源地、学制、专业、父母职业等方面，并没有显著性差异。然而，在成绩、母亲受教育程度、家庭收入等方面存在显著差异。同伴关系、教学制度、师生关系是影响本科生就读体验的重要因素。此外，学校环境、个体期望、个人经历等因素也会影响本科生的就读体验。
在成绩方面，学生的学业成绩与他们的就读体验存在明显差异。成绩较好的学生在各个维度上得分较高，表现出更高的积极性和投入度.在母亲受教育程度方面，母亲受教育程度高的学生在中外合作大学的就读体验得分更高。这表明母亲的受教育程度对学生的教育方式、家庭环境等方面有积极影响。

同伴关系、教学制度、师生关系等因素会对本科生的就读体验产生影响。良好的同伴关系可以提供支持和社交机会，积极的教学制度可以促进学习效果，良好的师生关系可以提供指导和支持。学校环境、个体期望、个人经历也会对本科生的就读体验产生影响。学校环境包括学术资源、国际交流机会等，可以扩展学生的视野。个体期望是指个人对学习和生活环境的期望，而个人经历则是个体在学校中的具体体验和遭遇。在家庭收入方面，不同家庭收入水平的学生在收获评价和就读体验上存在显著性差异。家庭收入较高的学生在这两个维度上得分较高，而其他维度上的差异不明显。

宁波诺丁汉大学实现课程国际化的方法如下：通过培养学生的国际品性，包括开放性、包容性等，使学生能够更加关注世界大事和全球问题。在课程中注重传授与国际接轨的专业知识，使学生具备与国际接轨的能力。结合中西方对同一问题的不同认识，让学生了解不同观点，培养其对文化差异的理解和评判能力。提供国际性的社团活动或实践活动，为学生提供发展国际品性的机会。增加中国文化相关课程的广度和深度，让学生加深对本民族文化的理解。

宁波诺丁汉大学在课程国际化方面具有以下特点和状况：在国际品性方面，宁波诺丁汉大学注重培养学生对世界的开放性和文化差异的包容性。学校的课程能够促使学生更加关注世界大事和全球问题，并使他们愿意与来自不同文化背景的人合作。调查结果显示，超过90%的学生认为学校的课程在某种程度上发展了其国际品性。在国际知识方面，宁波诺丁汉大学的专业课程能够与国际接轨，并结合中西方对同一问题的不同认识。调查结果显示，超过93%的学生认为专业课程中的知识与国际接轨。宁波诺丁汉大学的课程培养学生对国际问题的敏感性，加深学生对本民族文化的理解，并兼顾了国际性对内、对外的两个维度。调查结果显示，大部分学生认为通过在学校课程学习，他们更加关注世界大事和全球问题，对本民族的文化有了更深刻的认识。宁波诺丁汉大学的课程还通过社团活动或实践活动提供国际性的机会，为学生提供发展国际品性的空间。调查结果显示，学校的国际性社团活动或实践活动较多，为学生培养国际品性提供了机会。

中国文化课的深度还需要在以下几个方面进行提高：深入分析中国历史：目前中国文化课中有关中国历史的内容许多还停留在对史实的介绍上，缺乏深入的分析。未来的中国文化课可以从文化学、哲学、政治学等学科的视角来阐述事实，激发学生对相关问题的思考，加深对中国历史的理解。强化文化学、哲学等学科的内容：除了传授与中国文化有关的知识外，中国文化课还可以通过引入文化学、哲学等学科的视角，对中国文化进行更深入的探讨。这样可以帮助学生从更多的角度理解和思考中国文化的核心理念和价值观。结合实践活动和课外活动：除了正式的课堂教学，通过多种社会实践和课外活动的形式将中国文化传递给学生，可以使学生更好地理解和体验中国文化的精神。同时，可以结合学生的学习和生活实际，丰富中国文化课的内容，使其更具吸引力和实用性。请注意，以上回答是根据提供的信息进行推断和总结。如需准确和详细的信息，请参阅原始文档《课程国际化.pdf》。

为了加强国内外师生交流，可以采取以下措施：提高国际生比例：可以考虑适当增加国际生比例，为中国学生创造更多与国际学生交流和互动的机会。通过增加国际生的比例，可以促进不同文化背景的学生之间的交流和理解。加强教师与学生的互动机会：教师应该关注中国学生，鼓励和引导他们与教师交流。尤其是外籍教师可以在课堂教学过程中为中国学生提供与他们互动的机会。此外，在分组时可以考虑学生的国籍问题，使中国学生有更多机会与国际学生一起学习，提升他们的国际沟通能力。丰富课外活动：通过组织丰富多样的课外活动，如志愿者活动、文化交流活动等，为国内外师生提供更多的交流机会。这样可以促进师生之间的互动和了解，加深彼此的跨文化交流和认知。请注意，以上回答是根据一份名为《课程国际化.pdf》的文档提供的信息进行推测。如果需要准确和详细的信息，请参阅原始文档。

中外合作大学国际化人才培养模式的特点主要包括以下几个方面：教学形式的国际化：中外合作大学通过改革教学形式来培养学生的国际化能力，例如在课堂教学中引入专门的国际化课程和教材，促使学生具备批判思维和终身学习能力。校园生活的国际化：中外合作大学通过丰富多样的课外活动和文化交流活动，为学生提供与国际学生交流和互动的机会，培养学生的国际视野和跨文化交流能力全面发展的培养模式：中外合作大学不仅注重学生的学术知识培养，还注重培养学生的综合素养，包括国际理解能力、沟通合作能力和全球意识等，使学生具备适应国际化环境的能力。强调跨文化交流：中外合作大学重视培养学生的跨文化交流能力，鼓励学生与来自不同文化背景的人进行沟通和合作，培养学生的国际沟通能力和全球意识。需要注意的是，以上回答是根据一份名为《人才培养.pdf》的文档提供的信息进行推测。如果需要准确和详细的信息，请参阅原始文档。
国际化人才应具备的核心素养包括自我管理、批判思维、问题解决、健康素养、终身学习、国家认同、人文素养、社会责任和跨文化交流。

According to 1, the University of Nottingham Ningbo China runs a Preliminary year of English for Academic Purposes (EAP) for the majority of its students. When students pass this foundation year, they progress onto their main degree subject where communicative ability in speaking and writing English is considered important to the extent that they are able to express content knowledge. The Centre for English Language Education (CELE) has a sub-division called the Continuing Support Centre (CSC) that holds voluntary workshops and seminars to aid students who are no longer required to pass specific English language assessments. Additionally, the article focuses on a case study of French language education at UNNC and how it has been shaped to improve communicative language competences and motivation.

According to 3, the European Language Portfolio (ELP) is used at UNNC to help students plan their learning, learn autonomously, seek and enhance intercultural experiences. The article describes how French language tutors at UNNC have used different tools to shape the French language curriculum to improve communicative language competences and motivation, including the use of the ELP. The article also mentions that the ELP is introduced to students gradually through an introductory section at the end of different sections of the textbook

According to 1, French language tutors at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China have used different tools to shape the French language curriculum to improve communicative language competences and motivation. These tools include a French reading book activity that highlights the difference between Chinese and Western approaches to learning and enhances linguistic competences, as well as French movies that have been put in place to motivate and improve the general and communicative language competences of students. The article also mentions that the French curriculum includes extra-study development and makes students aware of the key objectives of the European Language Portfolio

According to 1, the Continuing Support Centre (CSC) is a sub-division of the Centre for English Language Education (CELE) at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC). The CSC holds voluntary workshops and seminars to aid students who are no longer required to pass specific English language assessments. The article suggests that the CSC provides support to students who need to improve their English language skills to express content knowledge in their main degree subject.

According to 1, the University of Nottingham Ningbo China and Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University have different rationales, strategies, curricula, partnership, and orientation. The University of Nottingham Ningbo China takes liberal arts education as given and leans toward the convergence/globalization model, while Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University adopts a more or less empirical approach and finds itself closer to the borrowing/localization model by creating its own identity through the joint strengths of the two parent universities. One is devoted to undergraduate education with some selected graduate programs, while the other aspires to become a leading research university in science, engineering, and management. The academically weak partner for the University of Nottingham guarantees the latter’s control of the curriculum, whereas the equal academic strengths between the University of Liverpool and its Chinese partner, Xi’an Jiaotong University, results in somewhat shared control of the curriculum.

According to 5, British universities are pioneering academic partnerships in China by setting up their overseas campuses in the country. The University of Nottingham and the University of Liverpool are two examples of British universities that have established their campuses in China. These universities have become brand names in China, and their strategic goals for setting up their overseas campuses have been successful, as evidenced by the growing enrollment of Chinese students in these universities in Britain. The impact of these partnerships on the globalization of higher education is significant, as they represent successful models of globalization of higher education in China. They also demonstrate unique characteristics, despite the common emphasis on the western tradition of liberal arts education. The educational programs on these two campuses in China differ in the choice of location and the physical appearance of the facilities and landscape, which is consistent with their own, unique, academic visions.

According to 14, there are many benefits and challenges of joint ventures between Chinese and foreign universities. The benefits include generating additional tuition revenues and assets overseas, recruiting Chinese students to the home campus, enhancing social science and humanities research related to the culture, society, economy, politics, literature, and philosophy of China, and advancing knowledge in science, technology, and engineering through international collaboration in research. It can also promote mutual understanding between countries, cultures, societies, and peoples. The challenges include differences in governance, management, and mission strategy, as well as differences in goals and expectations between the two institutions. The proportion of representation by the source and cooperating institutions on the governing board varies in China, which may have a material impact on what the source and cooperating institutions see as the best for them, and also on what they may decide as the optimal outcome for the offspring institution. Additionally, the Chinese Ministry of Education has developed a set of rules and regulations on the presence and operation of foreign higher educational institutions in China, which foreign universities must comply with. To overcome these challenges, foreign universities wishing to have a successful campus in China must adopt a long-term strategic vision, learn ways of cooperation, and promote mutual benefits, regardless of how much importance they attach to governance or management control. 14

According to 5, the British universities overseas campuses in China have unique characteristics despite the common emphasis on the western tradition of liberal arts education. For example, the campuses in Ningbo and Suzhou have different physical appearances and facilities that are consistent with their own academic visions. Additionally, their Chinese partners represent two extremes in the Chinese educational echelon, with very different institutional missions, strengths, and purposes. The educational programs on these two campuses in China also demonstrate unique characteristics. For instance, the University of Nottingham in Ningbo China has an active research agenda on issues related to contemporary China and sustainable technology, while Duke University's campus in Kunshan focuses on environmental management and global health. 5

According to 14, joint ventures between Chinese and foreign universities can promote mutual understanding between countries, cultures, societies, and peoples in several ways. For example, they can enhance social science and humanities research related to the culture, society, economy, politics, literature, and philosophy of China, as well as advance knowledge in science, technology, and engineering through international collaboration in research. Additionally, foreign students can use the campuses as a base to observe and study China or to immerse themselves in a language and cultural environment. By bringing together students and faculty from different backgrounds and cultures, joint ventures can also foster cross-cultural communication and exchange, which can lead to greater mutual understanding and respect. Overall, joint ventures between Chinese and foreign universities can help to bridge cultural and linguistic divides and promote greater global cooperation and understanding. 14

According to 14, foreign universities face several challenges when setting up campuses in China. These challenges include the need to partner with a Chinese university, which can be difficult due to differences in institutional culture and governance structures, as well as the need to navigate complex regulations and bureaucratic processes. Additionally, foreign universities may face cultural and linguistic barriers when working with Chinese students and faculty, as well as challenges related to differences in academic standards and expectations. To address these challenges, foreign universities must adopt a long-term strategic vision, learn ways of cooperation, and promote mutual benefits, regardless of how much importance they attach to governance or management control. They must also work closely with their Chinese partners to develop effective communication and collaboration strategies, and invest in programs and initiatives that promote cross-cultural understanding and exchange. Finally, they must be willing to adapt to local conditions and regulations, and be patient and persistent in their efforts to establish a successful presence in China. 14

The University of Nottingham Ningbo, China (UNNC) was the first Sino-foreign university to open a campus in mainland China in 2004 1. The campus now holds approximately 6,600 students and 500 staff from 40 different countries 1. The University of Nottingham in the UK was founded in 1881 and was awarded a Royal Charter in 1948, becoming the University of Nottingham 5. The UK campus has four campuses and is comprehensive in its subject areas, including engineering, sciences, agriculture and veterinary sciences, arts, and medicine 5. UNNC has departments covering English, International Communications, Education, International Studies, Economics, Business, Computer Science, Environmental Sciences, as well as 8 Engineering degree subjects within 5 departments 5.

The MSc course in Engineering Surveying and Geodesy at UNNC is based on the long-standing pedigree of the University of Nottingham in the UK 1. The model used is to duplicate the activities conducted on the UK campus, in terms of equipment, facilities, and modules taught both at undergraduate and post-graduate levels 21. All activities have the same quality control as in the UK, and the taught courses have the same external examiners and examination meetings as the UK 21. The course allows students to learn about a rapidly changing field and gain practical skills and experience using the extensive facilities available, all done in a western style of education, as well as in English 21. UNNC is also continuing to support the students, even after graduation, through continued involvement with the RICS and ICES 21.

UNNC aims to increase the overall student number to 8,000 by 2020, with 20% of the students being non-Chinese and 15-20% being postgraduate students 9. The expansion will mainly focus on the Faculty of Science and Engineering, increasing the student numbers to approximately 40% of the total student population 9. UNNC also plans to build new infrastructure, including a new 24 storey accommodation block, a 1,000 seater auditorium, an International Conference Centre, a teaching and learning building, as well as a new building for the International Academy of Marine Economy 9. These expansions will provide more opportunities for students and staff, as well as enhance the learning experiences at the campus 9. Additionally, UNNC has received support from the Chinese government at local and national levels, which will help to further develop the university 9.
